title: Diwali Bank Holiday: Banks Close November 9 in Some Cities, November 10 in Others — Full RBI November List
excerpt: Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8. Banks close Monday, November 9 for Diwali, Lakshmi Puja and Govardhan Puja in cities including Jaipur, Kanpur and Lucknow, and Tuesday, November 10 for Bali Pratipada and Vikram Samvat New Year in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad and others.
body:
• There is no single Diwali bank holiday: Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, and branch closures roll across Monday, November 9 and Tuesday, November 10 depending on the city.
  • November 9: banks close for Diwali, Lakshmi Puja and Govardhan Puja in Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Imphal, Jaipur, Kanpur and Lucknow.
  • November 10: banks close for Bali Pratipada, Govardhan Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai and Nagpur.
  • November 11 brings Bhai Dooj closures in a third set of cities, and the second and fourth Saturdays — November 14 and 28 — close banks nationwide. Check your branch's RBI circle before travelling for paperwork.

The Diwali bank holiday question — November 9 or 10? — has a frustrating but simple answer: both, depending on where your branch is. Diwali and Lakshmi Puja fall on Sunday, November 8 this year, when banks are closed anyway, so the festival closures land on the following two weekdays, split by region, in the Reserve Bank of India's holiday calendar, according to Jagran Josh's RBI list.

The two Diwali days, city by city

"Check your branch's RBI circle before travelling for paperwork."

On Monday, November 9, banks close in Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Imphal and Jaipur, and in Kanpur and Lucknow, for Diwali, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Vishwakarma Day on the listings compiled from the RBI calendar. On Tuesday, November 10, banks close in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai and Nagpur for Bali Pratipada, Govardhan Puja, Lakshmi Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year, according to BoldSky's November list. Gangtok appears on both days — and again on November 11 — giving it three consecutive regional holidays.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DetdBrPAjT-/

On Wednesday, November 11, banks close in Gangtok, Imphal, Kanpur, Kolkata, Lucknow and Shimla for Lakshmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, Bhai Dooj and Chitragupt Jayanti. A family with accounts in both Mumbai and Lucknow, in other words, faces closures on different days in each city.

The rest of November

Beyond Diwali week: November 13 is the Wangala Festival in Shillong; November 14 is the second Saturday, closed nationwide; November 16 is Chhath Puja in Patna and Ranchi; November 20 is Igas-Bagwal in Dehradun; November 23 is Seng Kut Snem in Shillong; November 24 covers Guru Nanak Jayanti, Karthika Purnima and Rahas Purnima in several cities including New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Hyderabad circles; November 27 is Kanakadasa Jayanthi in Bengaluru; and November 28 is the fourth Saturday, closed nationwide, according to the RBI annual calendar reported by Mint.

What still works on a holiday

Branch closures do not stop digital banking: UPI, net banking, mobile apps and ATMs continue to operate, and NEFT and RTGS run through online channels on their usual schedules. What stops is anything needing a person at a counter — cheque clearing presentations, demand drafts, locker access, KYC updates and document attestation. If a remittance, property registration or NRI account task needs a branch visit in Diwali week, book it for the working day in your specific city, not the day that works in another state. When in doubt, your own bank's branch holiday notice is the final word, because state governments can add local holidays to the RBI list.
